title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 102: The Kakapo
passageHtml:
READING A2 (BAND 4.0) — BÀI 102

The Kakapo: A Special Night Parrot

Paragraph 1. New Zealand is home to a very unusual bird called the kakapo. It is a night parrot that lives in forests. For millions of years, there were no land mammals in New Zealand to hunt it. Because of this, the kakapo lost the ability to fly. Today, it is the heaviest parrot in the world. Adult males can weigh four kilograms. The kakapo uses its strong legs to walk and climb trees. It only uses its short wings for balance when it jumps from branches.

Paragraph 2. Long ago, the kakapo only had to hide from large birds, like the giant Haast's eagle. Those eagles hunted by sight. When danger was near, the kakapo stood completely still. Its green feathers helped it hide on the forest floor. Later, human settlers brought cats, rats, and stoats to New Zealand. These animals hunt by smell, not by sight. The kakapo has a strong, sweet smell. Standing still did not protect it, so the bird almost died out.

Paragraph 3. The kakapo also has unusual breeding habits. It does not breed every year. It only has babies every two to four years, when native rimu trees grow a lot of fruit. Mothers feed this healthy food to their chicks. In summer, male birds dig small holes on hilltops and make loud booming sounds to call females. The loud calls can travel for kilometres across the mountains.

Paragraph 4. In 1977, workers found fewer than 200 kakapos, and almost all of them were old males. To save the species, New Zealand moved every living kakapo to safe islands with no cats or rats. Scientists put small radios on the birds and used drones to help them breed. Thanks to this hard work, the number of kakapos grew from 51 in 1995 to more than 240 today.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage?
Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "It only uses its short wings for balance when it jumps from branches."
Đoạn 2: "The kakapo has a strong, sweet smell."
Đoạn 3: "when native rimu trees grow a lot of fruit." (a lot of = plenty of).
Đoạn 4: "moved every living kakapo to safe islands with no cats or rats."

q5.text: The Haast's eagle used its sense of smell to find kakapos.

steps: Đoạn 2: "Those eagles hunted by sight." (săn bằng mắt chứ không phải bằng khứu giác).

q6.text: The sounds made by male kakapos can be heard from far away.

steps: Đoạn 3: "The loud calls can travel for kilometres across the mountains."

q7.text: Most of the kakapos found in 1977 were young female birds.

steps: Đoạn 4: "almost all of them were old males." → Trái ngược với chim cái trẻ.

q8.text: Tourists can visit the safe islands to see kakapos in the wild.

steps: Đoạn 4: Bài chỉ nói chim được chuyển đến các đảo an toàn không có mèo và chuột, không đề cập khách du lịch có được phép tới tham quan hay không.
